name: Super-Resolution Trace
description: Detects traces of neural super-resolution upscaling applied to AI-generated images — SRGAN-type networks leave characteristic frequency-domain artifacts (Ledig et al., 2017).
mechanism:
This method identifies traces left by neural super-resolution (SR) networks when images are upscaled beyond their native resolution:

1. **Frequency-Domain Upscaling Signature**: Neural SR networks (SRGAN, ESRGAN, Real-ESRGAN) synthesize high-frequency details using learned upsampling filters — typically sub-pixel convolution (Shi et al., 2016) or transposed convolution. These produce characteristic spectral signatures: periodic peaks in the power spectrum at frequencies related to the upscaling factor. The method computes the 2D FFT magnitude spectrum and detects peaks at expected locations for common scale factors (2×, 4×, 8×). A spectral periodicity score quantifies the strength of these peaks relative to the expected 1/f spectral falloff.

2. **Hallucinated Detail Detection**: SR networks generate plausible but fabricated high-frequency details that don't exist in the original low-resolution input. The method analyzes the ratio of high-frequency energy (above Nyquist of the hypothesized original resolution) to total energy. Natural images that were never upscaled have a smooth spectral rolloff, while SR-processed images show an abrupt energy boost above the original Nyquist frequency. The method estimates the original resolution by finding the frequency at which the spectral characteristic changes slope.

3. **Checkerboard Artifact Analysis**: Transposed convolution layers in SR networks produce checkerboard artifacts — regular grid-like patterns caused by uneven overlap in the deconvolution operation (Odena et al., 2016). The method detects these by computing the autocorrelation of residual images (input minus Gaussian-smoothed version) and searching for periodic peaks at intervals matching common upscaling factors. Even when visually imperceptible, these artifacts remain detectable in the autocorrelation domain.

4. **GAN Fingerprint in SR Context**: SRGAN and similar adversarial SR networks leave GAN-specific spectral fingerprints in addition to upscaling artifacts. The method extracts the high-pass residual and analyzes its spectral characteristics for the periodic patterns characteristic of specific generator architectures. By comparing against a database of known SR network fingerprints, the method can identify which SR architecture was used and estimate the upscaling factor.
parameters:
FFT analysis window: full image
Scale factor detection: 2×, 3×, 4×, 8×
Spectral peak threshold: SNR > 3 dB above background
High-pass filter: Laplacian of Gaussian (σ = 1.0)
Autocorrelation search range: 2–16 pixels
Checkerboard detection threshold: peak-to-median ratio > 2.5
Minimum image size: 128×128 pixels
accuracy: 82–90% accuracy detecting SR-upscaled images when the upscaling factor is 4× or greater. Checkerboard artifacts detected with precision of 0.88 for transposed convolution networks. Sub-pixel convolution (PixelShuffle) networks detected with 79% accuracy. Performance decreases for 2× upscaling and for newer architectures using attention-based upsampling.
source: Ledig, C. et al. (2017). Photo-Realistic Single Image Super-Resolution Using a Generative Adversarial Network. Proceedings of CVPR, 4681–4690.
useCase: Detecting whether an image has been neural-upscaled to hide its true resolution. Identifying AI-generated images that use SR as a post-processing step. Estimating original image resolution before upscaling. Forensic analysis of image provenance and processing history.
strengths:
• Spectral analysis reliably detects periodic upscaling artifacts
• Can estimate the upscaling factor and original resolution
• Checkerboard detection is robust even at low artifact intensity
• Architecture-specific fingerprints enable SR network identification
• Complements other forensic methods — SR artifacts are independent of content
limitations:
• Newer SR methods (SwinIR, HAT) with attention-based upsampling produce fewer periodic artifacts
• JPEG compression can mask checkerboard artifacts at high compression ratios
• Images with naturally periodic textures may produce false positives in autocorrelation analysis
• Low upscaling factors (2×) produce subtle artifacts difficult to distinguish from interpolation
• Anti-aliasing post-processing can reduce detectability of spectral peaks
